questions.question: What OS analogy does MemGPT use to explain its memory architecture?
options: File systems (directories, files, inodes)
Virtual memory (RAM = main context, disk = external store, page fault = memory tool call)
Networking (buffers, packets, routing tables)
Processes (PID, fork, exec, wait)
questions.explanation: MemGPT (Packer et al., arXiv:2310.08560) maps context management to OS virtual memory: main context = RAM, external context = disk, memory tool calls = page faults, agent control loop = OS kernel.

questions.question: What is the 'interrupt pattern' in MemGPT?
options: The agent pauses all processing when an error occurs
The agent invokes a memory tool mid-conversation, the runtime executes it, and the result is spliced into the next turn
A user can interrupt the agent at any time during processing
The agent uses interrupts to signal completion of a long task
questions.explanation: The memory-as-interrupt pattern means the agent can invoke memory tools mid-conversation (like a Unix read() syscall), the runtime fetches the result, and it appears as a new observation in the next turn.

questions.question: What three production failure modes of context windows does MemGPT address?
options: Speed, accuracy, cost
Overflow, dilution, and persistence across sessions
Hallucination, bias, and toxicity
Latency, throughput, and reliability
questions.explanation: MemGPT addresses three context failure modes: overflow (context exceeds window), dilution (irrelevant content reduces attention quality within a window), and persistence (sessions start empty without external memory).

questions.question: What is 'memory poisoning' in the context of MemGPT?
options: The memory store running out of space
Attacker-controlled content being stored as a memory note and re-ingested by the agent in future sessions
The model overwriting important memories with new ones
Memory operations taking too long and slowing the agent
questions.explanation: Memory poisoning occurs when attacker-reachable content (from retrieved web pages, emails, etc.) gets written into archival memory and then re-ingested by the agent in subsequent sessions, enabling persistent prompt injection across sessions.

questions.question: Which of these is a canonical MemGPT memory tool?
options: database_query(sql)
archival_memory_search(query, top_k)
context_window_expand(tokens)
model_reload(checkpoint)
questions.explanation: MemGPT defines tools like core_memory_append, core_memory_replace, archival_memory_insert, archival_memory_search(query, top_k), and conversation_search(query) as its memory tool surface.

questions.question: Why does Mem0's 2025 paper show that a 128k context window still misses facts that a 4k window agent with external memory catches?
options: The 128k model is less capable than the 4k model
Large contexts dilute attention even within the window; external memory with targeted retrieval maintains precision
The 128k window has more bugs than the 4k window
External memory is always retrieved instantly while large contexts are slow
questions.explanation: Even within a 128k context window, attention dilutes as the context grows. A 4k window agent with external memory can retrieve specific facts precisely on demand, outperforming the larger but diluted context.
